finding.claim: StreamableHTTPTransport performs no Origin or Host validation, so a DNS-rebinding page can drive an unauthenticated locally-bound MCP server (initialize, then tools/call) and read results. Medium severity, conditional on deployment without auth.
finding.source: Cross-origin browser request after DNS rebinding; Content-Type application/json and Accept headers, which the attacker controls
finding.sink: handle_post -> handle_initialization (L646-699) and handle_regular_request (L713-740) dispatching tools/call

trace.note: handle_post begins; only Accept and Content-Type validated
initialize creates a new session with no caller authentication
handle_regular_request dispatches tools/call for the attacker's own session

finding.guards_checked: Accept header (L528-539), Content-Type (L547-557), Mcp-Session-Id (attacker creates its own session), MCP-Protocol-Version header. Grep of lib/ found no HTTP_ORIGIN, Origin or Host check.

finding.claim: Request body is read fully into memory with no size limit before any session validation, allowing memory exhaustion by an unauthenticated client. Low severity.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled HTTP POST body of arbitrary size

trace.note: session check happens only after the body is buffered

finding.guards_checked: Accept and Content-Type checks run first (L367-371) but do not bound size. No Content-Length or body-size limit anywhere in lib/.

finding.claim: Client sends the stored refresh token and client secret to whichever authorization server the MCP server's PRM names. The only AS check is HTTPS, and there is no AS pinning across flows. Impact is a malicious or compromised MCP server obtaining long-lived refresh tokens. Trust-boundary/hardening gap, medium-low.
finding.source: PRM authorization_servers[0] and WWW-Authenticate 401 response controlled by the MCP server
finding.sink: post_to_token_endpoint (flow.rb L674-737) with refresh_token (L178-183) and client_secret Basic auth (L696)

trace.note: attempt_refresh runs with stored refresh token
refresh_token form sent to AS token_endpoint

finding.guards_checked: HTTPS requirement (discovery.rb L181-194), PRM resource coverage (flow.rb L513-525, identifier only), issuer equality against the attacker-chosen discovery URL (flow.rb L402-412), PKCE on auth-code path. No AS pinning.

finding.claim: Client performs GETs to server-supplied HTTPS URLs (resource_metadata, authorization_servers) with no host, IP, or timeout restriction, a blind SSRF from the client's network position. Low severity; responses are not reflected.
finding.source: WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata parameter from the MCP server's 401 response
finding.sink: fetch_metadata_json -> http_get via default_http_client (flow.rb L785-794), no private-IP block

trace.note: resource_metadata URL checked only for HTTPS
errors rescued and swallowed, so response is blind
default Faraday client with no host/IP restriction or timeout

finding.guards_checked: Discovery.secure_url? HTTPS-only (discovery.rb L181-194). No private, loopback or metadata address block. Errors from fetch are not returned to the attacker.
